sources.title: Average bank interest rates for savings accounts, CDs and more

scenes.title: Your bank pays 0.38%
scenes.sub: That's the national average savings rate.

lines.say: The average savings account pays zero point three eight percent.
Some accounts pay about ten times that. Here's what it means in real dollars.
lines.show: Some accounts pay about 10 times that. Here's what it means in real dollars.

lines.say: Per the FDIC, the national average is zero point three eight percent a year.
lines.show: Per the FDIC, the national average is 0.38% a year.

lines.say: Some high-yield savings accounts pay around three point eight percent or more.
lines.show: Some high-yield savings accounts pay around 3.8% or more.

lines.say: On a thousand dollars for a year, that's three dollars eighty versus thirty eight dollars.
lines.show: On $1,000 for a year, that's $3.80 versus $38.

lines.say: On five thousand, it's one hundred ninety dollars versus nineteen.
Before you switch, check that it's FDIC or NCUA insured, with no monthly fees.
lines.show: Before you switch, check that it's FDIC or NCUA insured, with no monthly fees.

lines.say: And remember, savings rates can change at any time.
lines.show: And remember, savings rates can change at any time.

scenes.takeaway: Same money, more interest. Check your savings rate today.
